ESP32 and Arduino IDE — practical experience

I have worked with many ESP boards and know their everyday quirks: selecting the correct board and port, libraries, pins, power and communication. In Kora, the ESP32-C6 handles the neck, light sensors, GPIO and communication with Raspberry Pi, while the radio runs on an ESP32-S3.

On Raspberry Pi 5, I bring together cameras, lidar, sensors, neck control, speech, memory and the operator panel. My work covers hardware selection, integration, commissioning, measurements and testing the complete system.

I do not present Python as a language I have mastered independently. I develop the code with programming-support tools; my role covers requirements, integration with real hardware, testing, diagnostics and decisions about corrections.
Models run locally on my hardware and connect to Kora through her own services. I test their speed, response quality, memory and the division of work between conversation and vision.
Hailo is intended to accelerate local image analysis and person tracking. The hardware is part of the project, but I honestly describe this layer as being integrated and tested rather than finished.

I built the wooden slatted body by hand, then combined it with a bought flower-shaped shade and my own ESP32-C3 SuperMini-based controller.
The lamp in the workshop — its hand-built wooden slatted body is clearly visible behind Kora.

The lamp uses 130 RGB LEDs split into two independently controlled zones. One hundred LEDs in the lower section create vertical effects inside the wooden structure, while thirty LEDs in the crown illuminate the flower with a different colour and animation. This means the lower section can glow blue while the shade is red at the same time. I change the colours and effects in software.
The blue lower section and red crown demonstrate independent control of both zones.

This is a ready-to-use example for popular WS2812B strips using the FastLED library. The lower 100 LEDs display a moving rainbow, while the 30 LEDs in the crown independently change colour and gently pulse. The GPIO numbers are examples and must be adjusted to match your own wiring before uploading.
data signal for the 100 lower LEDs
data signal for the 30 crown LEDs
common ground for the ESP32 and LED power supply
library installed through the Arduino IDE

Important: 130 LEDs must not be powered from an ESP32 board pin. The strips require a separate, correctly sized power supply, a common ground and protection. At 5 V, the theoretical maximum for 130 LEDs can approach 7.8 A at full white. A 330–470 Ω resistor is recommended on the data line; if control is unreliable, also use a 3.3 V to 5 V logic-level shifter.

How the project can start funding itself
Kora remains a personal project and is not for sale. Verified technical materials, CNC work and voluntary support can help fund the work — without promising things that are not ready yet.

They will be based only on solutions I have actually built, measured and documented. The first planned item is a bilingual PDF about safely powering a multi-servo robot — pricing will appear only after the document and measurements are complete.

You can enquire about a simple part, sign or relief similar to the work shown in this portfolio. Include dimensions, material, quantity and a sketch or file. I will check feasibility first and only then provide an individual quote.

The videos show real stages, tests, corrections and finished work. The channel does not pretend to advertise a finished product — it points viewers to the portfolio and the catalogue of parts used in the projects.
